overview: Solo Eso shares his unique rows with Eso & Kechizu. They tune summon orders, the decay beam, and its cameras.
technicalOverview: CN_260 (Eso) uses the CP_160 action controller: a shikigami-order character whose cursed-energy attacks either command shikigami 0 (ATTACKG) or fire/decay beams through ATTACKH, with RotTechnique/decay as a separate mode. AGameCharacter reads these as UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[ValueIndex] with no bounds check; CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterUnique supplies the row order, so these are literal zero-based indices. The seven populated rows are one shared behavior row, one order row, one beam/charge row, one decay/drain row, and three identical level-selected camera rows. Only AGameCharacter's CharacterUnique rows are documented here; CN_080's own unique floats belong to AGameShikigami's ShikigamiUniqueDataTable.

CP_160.title: Shared shikigami and beam settings
CP_160.overview: Default row for automatic/manual shikigami orders and the beam growth multiplier. It is fixed row 0 for every CP_160 unique read shown below.

0.label: Beam growth factor
0.simple: How quickly the cursed-energy beam extends when shikigami 0 cannot provide its shortcut.
0.technical: AddBeam starts Factor at 1 only when shikigami 0 exists and its interface IsDefeated() is true; if shikigami 0 is missing or not defeated, Factor = owner unique(0,0). OnEffectPlayed passes the level-specific Rate and AddBeam stores Entry.Rate = Factor * Rate. TickBeams grows Progress by (DeltaTime / (CustomTimeDilation > 0 ? CustomTimeDilation : 1)) * Entry.Rate and clamps to [0, MaxProgress]. Generic readers of the same slot also exist (AI timed-hold base duration, secondary-target steering divisor, ProjectionSorceryReceive fallback), but no CP_160-specific route to those was traced; CP_160's default AI factory creates the plain CursedEnergyAttack actions, not the timed-hold actions.

1.label: Shikigami auto-attack range
1.simple: How close shikigami 0 must be to Eso before Eso will order its auto attack, and how far away an opponent may be.
1.technical: TickAutoAttack reads unique(1,0) both for the owner-to-shikigami distance gate (Delta.Size() > Range returns) and for the opponent search radius (candidate distance > Range skipped). There is no negative-value exception here. A generic CursedEnergyAttack1Hold AI action adds row0[1] * cursed-energy level to row0[0], but CP_160's base behavior controller does not create that timed-hold action.

2.label: Auto-attack hold time
2.simple: How long a valid target must be available before the automatic shikigami command is issued.
2.technical: AutoAttackTime accumulates scaled DeltaTime; TickAutoAttack returns while unique(2,0) > AutoAttackTime, so the command fires on the first tick with elapsed strictly greater than the value (equality still waits). Failed gates reset AutoAttackTime to 0. Generic CursedEnergyAttack2Hold uses row0[2] * level + row0[0] as a hold duration, but CP_160's AI factory does not create that action.

3.label: Auto-attack cooldown
3.simple: Pause after one automatic shikigami attack before another can be issued.
3.technical: After SetTargetMode, AutoAttackCooldown is set to unique(3,0). It is decremented by scaled DeltaTime only while >0, and a new auto attack requires AutoAttackCooldown <= 0. A shikigami summon-cooldown restart instead sets the timer to -1.0f.

4.label: Default order radius
4.simple: How close the shikigami must get to the queued target before a normal order attack starts.
4.technical: TickAutoAttack and TickOrderAttack pass unique(4,0) as Value194 to UCN_080_ActionController::SetTargetMode(2, Attack_3, Value194, Value198, ...). CN_080 stores it as QueuedActionRadius; while not attacking and radius >= 0, reaching the target within that distance triggers the queued attack. Stick-up paths replace this with row0[7].

5.label: Default order timeout
5.simple: How long the shikigami keeps the normal order target mode before giving it up.
5.technical: unique(5,0) is passed as Value198 to CN_080::SetTargetMode and stored as TargetModeTimeLimit. CN_080 counts it down when >=0 and calls ResetTargetMode after it goes negative if no attack is active. Stick-up paths replace this with row0[8].

6.label: Manual order range
6.simple: Maximum owner-to-shikigami distance for the player-triggered shikigami order.
6.technical: TickOrderAttack reads unique(6,0) as Range, then returns if Range >= 0 and the 3D owner-to-shikigami distance is greater than Range; a negative value disables this range culling. This gate is checked before the AttackSet row is looked up and before the cursed-energy cost is applied.

7.label: Stick-up order radius
7.simple: Queued-attack radius used when the player holds up on the stick during a manual order.
7.technical: When IsLeftStickInDirection(0, 45.0001, 0.5) is true, TickOrderAttack switches the action to Attack_4 and passes unique(7,0) as Value194 (QueuedActionRadius) to CN_080::SetTargetMode. Otherwise row0[4] and Attack_3 are used.

8.label: Stick-up order timeout
8.simple: Target-mode timeout used when the player holds up on the stick during a manual order.
8.technical: With the same stick-up condition, unique(8,0) is passed as Value198 (TargetModeTimeLimit) to CN_080::SetTargetMode; otherwise row0[5] is used. Expiry is handled by CN_080's ActionTick.

9.label: Stick-up manual order range
9.simple: Owner-to-shikigami distance limit for the up-stick manual order.
9.technical: TickOrderAttack replaces Range with unique(9,0) when the stick is up; the same gate applies: Range >= 0 and distance > Range returns, while a negative value disables the limit. Down-stick has no special range entry in this row.

10.label: Order energy multiplier
10.simple: How much of the chosen attack row's cursed-energy cost Eso pays when ordering the shikigami.
10.technical: TickOrderAttack computes CursedEnergy = unique(10,0) * AttackRow->CursedEnergy_Add + current cursed energy. When StateCondition_IsCursedEnergyNotForce(AttackRow) is true and the result is <0, the order is refused; otherwise the computed value is written to the status controller after the order is issued.

notes.text: Row 0 also supplies the fallback duration for FGameCharacterAction_ProjectionSorceryReceive when a damage row is absent; that generic receive action is not a CP_160-specific consumer.

The AI timed-hold readers of row 0 indices 0/1/2 belong to CursedEnergyAttack1Hold/2Hold. CP_160 has its own think node but no dedicated behavior controller (BrainCreate95 default), so those Hold actions are not in its factory.

CP_160_ATTACKG.title: CE 1 shikigami-order (ATTACKG) targeting
CP_160_ATTACKG.overview: Values for the CursedEnergyAttack_1 family: which ATTACKG variant is chosen and the radius/timeout handed to the shikigami's queued target mode.

0.label: Neutral order radius
0.simple: How close the shikigami must get before the neutral CE 1 order attack starts.
0.technical: CE_1 StartAttackHoming and the auto-attack branch read unique(0,1) as Value194 and pass it to CN_080::SetTargetMode as QueuedActionRadius. The auto branch also uses row1[1] as Value198.

1.label: Neutral order timeout
1.simple: How long the neutral CE 1 queued target mode lasts.
1.technical: unique(1,1) is passed as Value198 to CN_080::SetTargetMode and stored as TargetModeTimeLimit; CN_080 resets the target mode after it expires when no attack is active.

2.label: Neutral order range
2.simple: Maximum shikigami-to-owner distance for the neutral ATTACKG order.
2.technical: GetAttackSetRow starts with Id CP_160_ATTACKG and Range = unique(2,1); with shikigami 0 alive, orderable and a valid target, it falls back to CP_160_ATTACKG_5 when Range >= 0 and the owner-to-shikigami distance exceeds Range. Negative Range means no distance fallback.

3.label: Up-stick order radius
3.simple: Queued-attack radius for the up-stick ATTACKG_2 order.
3.technical: When the stick is up, CE_1 StartAttackHoming and the auto-attack branch replace Value194 with unique(3,1), along with Attack_2 as the debuff byte in manual CE_1, and pass it to CN_080::SetTargetMode.

4.label: Up-stick order timeout
4.simple: Target-mode timeout for the up-stick ATTACKG_2 order.
4.technical: When the stick is up, unique(4,1) is passed as Value198 (TargetModeTimeLimit) to CN_080::SetTargetMode instead of row1[1].

5.label: Up-stick order range
5.technical: GetAttackSetRow sets Id to CP_160_ATTACKG_2 and Range to unique(5,1) when the stick is up; the same >= 0 / distance > Range fallback test selects CP_160_ATTACKG_5 when out of range.

6.label: Unresolved ATTACKG value
6.simple: A non-zero value (500) with no traced CP_160 reader.
6.technical: No CP_160 code path was found that reads row 1 index 6. The nearby ATTACKG selection reads indices 2, 5 and 7 for ranges and indices 0/1/3/4 for SetTargetMode parameters; this index is therefore recorded as unresolved rather than assigned a meaning from its magnitude.

7.label: Down-stick order range
7.simple: Maximum owner-to-shikigami distance for the down-stick ATTACKG_4 order.
7.technical: GetAttackSetRow sets Id to CP_160_ATTACKG_4 and Range to unique(7,1) when the stick is down; exceeding that range (when non-negative) selects CP_160_ATTACKG_5. CE_1 StartAttackHoming's down-stick branch does not read row1[7]; it sets Mode 1, Value194 = -1 and Value198 = -1 instead.

notes.text: CP_160_ATTACKG_5 is the fallback for shikigami defeat, missing target or out-of-range; StartAttackHoming returns before SetTargetMode for that set, so no unique targeting values are passed.
GetGuardDamageRate reports the active ATTACKG variant as 0/1/2/3 for ATTACKG/_2/_3/_4 and -1 otherwise; this is row-name dispatch, not a unique float read.

CP_160_ATTACKH.title: CE 2 beam aim, growth and level-3 charge
CP_160_ATTACKH.overview: OnEffectPlayed selects beam aim/growth/clamp values by cursed-energy level from this row; TickAttack uses index 9 for the level-3 held charge. This row, not ATTACKH_2, is the beam tuning row.

0.label: Level 1 beam turn limit
0.simple: Maximum turn toward the secondary target for a level 1 beam shot.
0.technical: OnEffectPlayed uses unique(0,2) as MaxAngle for FX_CP_160_08111/08121/08131 when level is 1 or unrecognised (default/case 1). Planar yaw and elevation are clamped to +/-MaxAngle before the effect is rotated; CursedEnergyAttack_2_Auto/Air_2_Auto override MaxAngle to 90 degrees.

1.label: Level 2 beam turn limit
1.simple: Maximum turn toward the secondary target for a level 2 beam shot.
1.technical: OnEffectPlayed case 2 reads unique(1,2) as MaxAngle for the same clamp; auto types still override it to 90 degrees.

2.label: Level 3 beam turn limit
2.simple: Maximum turn toward the secondary target for a level 3 beam shot.
2.technical: OnEffectPlayed case 3 reads unique(2,2) as MaxAngle; auto types still override it to 90 degrees.

3.label: Level 1 beam growth rate
3.simple: How fast the level 1 beam extends each frame.
3.technical: OnEffectPlayed passes unique(3,2) as Rate to AddBeam; AddBeam stores Factor * Rate and TickBeams adds (DeltaTime / (CustomTimeDilation > 0 ? CustomTimeDilation : 1)) * Rate to Progress. No explicit unit name is in the source; it is a per-scaled-second progress increment.

4.label: Level 2 beam growth rate
4.simple: How fast the level 2 beam extends each frame.
4.technical: Case 2 passes unique(4,2) as Rate through the same AddBeam/TickBeams growth calculation.

5.label: Level 3 beam growth rate
5.simple: How fast the level 3 beam extends each frame.
5.technical: Case 3 passes unique(5,2) as Rate through the same AddBeam/TickBeams growth calculation.

6.label: Level 1 beam maximum progress
6.simple: How far the level 1 beam can grow.
6.technical: Case 1 passes unique(6,2) as MaxProgress; TickBeams clamps Progress to [0, MaxProgress] and the final value is written to the spawned effect's BeamEndPoint and used for the beam capsules.

7.label: Level 2 beam maximum progress
7.simple: How far the level 2 beam can grow.
7.technical: Case 2 passes unique(7,2) as MaxProgress with the same clamp and final beam handling.

8.label: Level 3 beam maximum progress
8.simple: How far the level 3 beam can grow.
8.technical: Case 3 passes unique(8,2) as MaxProgress with the same clamp and final beam handling.

9.label: Level 3 charge repeat interval
9.simple: How long Eso holds the level 3 CE 2 attack before paying the cost and replaying it while the button stays held.
9.technical: TickAttack, level 3, start count 1: after Flag158 and affordability gates and while CursedEnergyAttack_2 is held, ActionElapsedTime += DeltaTime; the tick returns while ActionElapsedTime <= unique(9,2). On the first tick with elapsed > value it applies CursedEnergy_Add, resets the timer and replays the attack animation; releasing or failing affordability sets Flag159.

notes.text: Beam growth is time-dilation adjusted and the beam trace clips Length at the first non-passing contact before Niagara and capsule updates; dead entries spawn the row-Id effect at the final beam transform.
Level 3 charge timing uses row 2 index 9, while the level 1/2/3 shot cameras come from rows 4/5/6; the two mechanisms are separate.

CP_160_ATTACKH_2.title: Decay search radius and energy drain
CP_160_ATTACKH_2.overview: Despite the ATTACKH_2 name, the traced CP_160 reads of this row are the decay-opponent search radius and the cursed-energy drain rate while decay mode is active.

0.label: Decay opponent search radius
0.simple: How far away an opponent with a decay/rot stack can be and still count for Eso's decay mechanic.
0.technical: GetDecayingOpponents reads unique(0,3) as Range; if Range >= 0 and the opponent-to-owner distance is greater than Range, that opponent is skipped. A negative value (the exported -1) disables the distance cutoff. The same list is used by CE_2 CanCancelCurrent and StartAttackHoming and by AI state condition 0x55.

1.label: Decay-mode cursed-energy drain
1.simple: Cursed energy lost per second while Eso is in decay mode.
1.technical: GetCursedEnergyDrainRate returns 0 when bDecayMode == 0, otherwise unique(1,3). AGameCharacter::GetActionValue113 forwards that value and GameCharacterStatusController subtracts Drain * DeltaTime when Drain >= 0 (no subtraction for negative values).

notes.text: A generic JugonStunReceive Start reads the attacker's row 3 indices 5-8 for distance-interpolated stun duration, but no CP_160-specific route to those indices was traced; the exported values there are zero and are left untraced.

Decay mode picks Decay_1/2/3 stacks rather than RotTechnique; SetDecayMode(0) strips those decay stacks from opponents, and ActionTick turns decay off unless an opponent still has a stack while Eso attacks or holds cursed energy.

CP_160_ATTACKH_SHOOT_CAMERA_1.title: Level 1 shot camera
CP_160_ATTACKH_SHOOT_CAMERA_1.overview: Used when the cursed-energy level is 1. All three exported camera rows have identical values; indices 0-10 are read by the shared MakeUniqueCameraRequest when camera mode 2 is entered.

0.label: Camera offset X
0.simple: Camera position offset along the gaze-space forward axis for this shot.
0.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest(2, 4) sets Request.CameraOffset.X = unique(0,4); mode 2 places the camera at eye base + GazeRotation.Quaternion().RotateVector(CameraOffset).

1.label: Camera offset Y
1.simple: Camera position offset along the gaze-space side axis.
1.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest(2, 4) sets Request.CameraOffset.Y = unique(1,4); the same gaze-space rotation applies.

2.label: Camera offset Z
2.simple: Camera position offset along the gaze-space up axis.
2.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest(2, 4) sets Request.CameraOffset.Z = unique(2,4); the same gaze-space rotation applies.

3.label: Downward gaze limit
3.simple: How far below the eye the camera may look when aimed at the target.
3.technical: unique(3,4) becomes Request.LimitAngleDown. In mode 2, when the gaze target is below the eye, elevation above this limit is rotated back to it; the limit is an angle in degrees.

4.label: Upward gaze limit
4.simple: How far above the eye the camera may look when aimed at the target.
4.technical: unique(4,4) becomes Request.LimitAngleUp; it clamps elevation when the gaze target is above the eye.

5.label: Field of view
5.simple: How wide the camera view is during this shot.
5.technical: unique(5,4) becomes Request.FieldOfView. On a camera-mode change a value > 0 starts FOV interpolation when the blend time is > 0, otherwise the FOV snaps. CP_160 overrides the FOV to 90 when returning from mode 2, so this row's value applies to entering the shot view.

6.label: FOV blend time
6.simple: How long the field-of-view change takes.
6.technical: unique(6,4) becomes Request.FieldOfViewBlendTime; values > 0 start FovInterp, values <= 0 snap the FOV.

7.label: FOV easing selector
7.simple: Which easing curve the field-of-view blend uses.
7.technical: unique(7,4) is cast to int and mapped: 0 Linear, 1 EaseIn, 2 EaseOut, 3 EaseInOut; other values leave the default. The exported 3 selects EaseInOut.

8.label: Gaze orbit yaw
8.simple: Yaw rotation of the gaze point around the camera.
8.technical: unique(8,4) becomes Request.OrbitYaw; FRotator(OrbitPitch, OrbitYaw, 0) rotates the gaze point about the camera when the orbit is non-zero.

9.label: Gaze orbit pitch
9.simple: Pitch rotation of the gaze point around the camera.
9.technical: unique(9,4) becomes Request.OrbitPitch in the same gaze-orbit rotator.

10.label: Camera roll
10.simple: Roll applied to the final view.
10.technical: unique(10,4) becomes Request.Roll and is passed to SetViewTarget87 with the camera location and gaze target.

notes.text: StartAttackHoming selects this row for level 1; UniqueAction parameter 10 re-creates the same request when restoring from camera mode 2.
MakeUniqueCameraRequest fills only indices 0-10 for mode 2 and returns a default request for other modes; no CP_160 code reads this camera row's indices 11-13.

MakeUniqueCameraRequest fills only indices 0-10 for mode 2 and returns a default request for other modes; no CP_160 code reads this camera row's indices 11-13.

The CE_2 beam values come from row 2 (ATTACKH): aim angles, growth rates and max progress are indexed by cursed-energy level; the shot camera rows are separate and selected by level in StartAttackHoming.

Decay mode changes both opponent filtering and which actions are allowed: GetDecayingOpponents uses row 3 index 0, CE_2 attacks using ATTACKH_2/_3 sets require a decaying opponent, and RotTechnique is converted to DEBUFF_DECAY_<level> while the mode flips on.

Shikigami commands are delegated to CN_080_ActionController::SetTargetMode; CP_160 supplies radius, timeout, mode and queued action. CN_080's own unique-float calls use AGameShikigami's ShikigamiUniqueDataTable, not these CP_160 rows.
ATTACKG variants are stick-sensitive: up selects _2 with row 1 index 5 range, down selects _4 with row 1 index 7 range, and any gate failure falls back to ATTACKG_5 which skips target-mode setup.

The level-3 camera request is only installed at attack start count 0; the third start restores the saved mode with FOV 90. UniqueAction parameter 10 does the same restore. If the level is outside 1-3 while camera mode is 2, RowIndex stays -1 and is passed to MakeUniqueCameraRequest unsanitized.
Beams are released newest-first when character-specific state resets, and the tick removes dead entries after spawning the final effect at the clamped beam endpoint.
The unchecked accessor itself is at AGameCharacter::GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue; the shared verification note records the same raw deref and the inlining caveats around its callers.
